auth.text: Every call sends Authorization: Bearer <event API key>. A key belongs to exactly one Robert event, so no path names the event. Alchemize treats a key that doesn't start with ysws_ as missing, so event keys apparently carry that prefix. Calls with a body send Content-Type: application/json.

errors.text: A failed call answers with a non-2xx status and a JSON body whose message field is a human-readable reason. The clients show message and fall back to the status code when it is missing.

states.meaning: A new project waits in awaiting_review for a fraud reviewer's 1 to 10 score. A score above 4 moves it to awaiting_outcome until the program records its own decision. A score of 4 or below moves it to rejected_fraud, which is final. A recorded outcome makes it decided.

score_bands.meaning: A final rejection. Carnival dismisses the project.
Usually a deduction. In Carnival the granting admin must acknowledge it, which is Carnival's own step.

project.description: The project object GET /projects/:id returns and GET /projects lists.

fields.name: id
fields.meaning: Robert's id. Alchemize refuses to put anything but a UUID in a path.

fields.name: externalId
fields.meaning: The program's own id, as sent on create.

fields.name: trustScore
fields.meaning: The fraud reviewer's score, null until there is one.

fields.name: review
fields.meaning: {trustScore, note, at}: the score, the reviewer's note or null, and when.

fields.name: outcome
fields.meaning: {status, reason, at}: approved or rejected, the reason or null, and when. See disagreements for pixl's longer reading.

fields.name: creditedSeconds
fields.meaning: Robert's own credited time, worked out from the Hackatime project names it was sent. It is Robert's figure for fraud scoring, not the program's hours.

body.name: kind
body.meaning: hackatime projects carry hackatimeProjects. hardware projects carry journal instead.

body.name: demoUrl
body.meaning: Left out by Alchemize and pixl when there is none. trmnt sends an empty string instead.

body.name: submitter
body.meaning: {slackId, hackatimeId}. Each client sends the Slack id; hackatimeId is a number, sent when known.

body.name: hackatimeProjects
body.meaning: The Hackatime project names Robert credits time from. Robert caps the list at 50 distinct names. This is Robert's only time-bearing input.

body.name: journal
body.meaning: For hardware: [{title, content, loggedAt, hours}], hours optional.

body.name: externalId
body.meaning: The program's id for this submission. Sending the same externalId again returns the same Robert project instead of a new one, so retries are safe. pixl puts the ship time in it so that each new ship gets its own record.

endpoints.returns: {id, state, created}. created tells a new project from an earlier one returned for the same externalId.

notes.text: Alchemize sends nothing about a person beyond the Slack id and the Hackatime id: never an email, name, address, birthdate or Unified ID.

endpoints.returns: The project object. See disagreements for the wrapper trmnt expects.

query.name: state
query.meaning: One of states.values. Every client asks for one state at a time.

query.name: limit
query.meaning: Page size. Carnival and pixl ask for 100.

endpoints.returns: {total, projects}: the event's projects in that state, newest submission first, and how many there are in all.

notes.text: pixl polls this list for awaiting_outcome, rejected_fraud and decided, because webhooks alone miss scores in the 5 to 10 range and carry no review note.

body.name: reason
body.meaning: Sent only when there is one.

errors.text: Allowed only while the project is awaiting_outcome. 409 once the outcome is final, most often because Robert already rejected it as fraud.

body.name: signedOffBy
body.meaning: Who on the program's side approved the withdrawal.

errors.text: 409 once a fraud reviewer has scored the project.

body.name: webhookUrl
body.meaning: Where Robert should send the event's webhooks. null clears it.

endpoints.returns: {webhookUrl, secret}: the secret webhook.json's signatures are keyed with.

disagreements.text: trmnt reads GET /projects/:id as {project: {...}}, while Carnival and Alchemize read the project object at the top level. One of them is wrong, or Robert sends both. A compatible client should accept either.

pixl types a listed project's outcome as {status, reason, trustScore, reviewedAt, reviewerName}, while Carnival and Alchemize type it as {status, reason, at}. The webhook's outcome has trustScore and reviewedAt (webhook.json), so the list may carry the longer form.
